categories.headline: Weakest area: visual hierarchy (2/5).

findings.title: Cookie consent modal blocks the page and competes with the main content
findings.evidence: A large white modal covers the center of the viewport. It holds about 20 lines of dense legal text in small type. The rest of the page is dimmed, and the nav items (Appliances…, Week), the product headline, and the hero phone images are cut off behind it. The three buttons (Configure, Accept All, Decline All) sit at the bottom of the text block, with a large empty white area below them.
findings.fix: Use a compact bottom banner or a smaller modal. Put a short summary at the top, give the buttons equal weight, and move the long legal text behind a 'Learn more' link. Remove the empty space at the bottom of the modal. The page should stay usable and visible.
findings.impact: Visitors decide in seconds; unclear hierarchy and actions send them to a competitor.

findings.title: Cookie buttons look nearly identical, and the primary page CTA is weak
findings.evidence: 'Accept All' and 'Decline All' are both solid dark-blue pills of the same size and weight, and 'Configure' is an outline pill. Users have to read each label to tell them apart. On the page itself, the 'Buy' button is a small blue pill at the far right, next to the price text ('From £27.25/mo. or £654.00 with trade-in**'). It is easy to miss, and the dense footnote marker adds clutter.
findings.fix: Give the consent actions a clear order of importance, with Accept as the primary and Decline as secondary but equally easy to find. Enlarge the 'Buy' CTA and place it next to a clear price. Keep a sticky Buy button in view as the user scrolls.
findings.impact: Visitors decide in seconds; unclear hierarchy and actions send them to a competitor.

findings.title: The top region is cluttered, with competing layers and ambiguous labels
findings.evidence: A region selector bar ('…nited Kingdom' with a dropdown and a 'Continue' button, plus a close X) sits above the main header. Below it are Support / For Business links, the main nav, a product sub-nav (Galaxy S26 Ultra, S26+ | S26 | S26 FE), and a tabs row (Features, Compare, Gifts and Savings, Reviews). Further down, a truncated banner reads 'Guarante…' and '…rtphone²'. The pricing block shows 'From £49.13/mo. or £1,179.00' in a cramped two-line layout.
findings.fix: Dismiss the region banner automatically after the user confirms, or collapse it into the footer. Cut the number of stacked navigation layers above the fold. Tidy the price display with a clear monthly vs. full-price format and reduce the footnote symbols.
findings.impact: Visitors decide in seconds; unclear hierarchy and actions send them to a competitor.
